quiz.question: Why is a PIR sensor called 'passive'?

answers.answer: Because it requires no power to operate
Because it does not send out any signal of its own; it only detects existing infrared radiation
Because it can only detect stationary objects
Because it uses a passive resistor instead of an active transistor

quiz.explanation: A PIR sensor is called passive because it does not emit any signal. It only senses changes in the infrared radiation already present in its environment.

quiz.question: What does a PIR sensor actually detect to sense motion?

answers.answer: Visible light changes when something moves
Sound waves reflected off moving objects
Changes in infrared radiation caused by a warm body moving across its field of view

quiz.explanation: PIR sensors have two infrared-sensitive slots behind a Fresnel lens. When a warm body moves, one slot sees more IR than the other, triggering a HIGH output.

quiz.question: What extra components does a PIR sensor need to connect to a Raspberry Pi?

answers.answer: A voltage divider and an ADC
An external library and a pull-up resistor
None, just power, ground, and one data pin
A Fresnel lens adapter and a signal amplifier

quiz.explanation: PIR sensors are wired very simply: just power, ground, and one data pin. No voltage dividers, ADC, or special libraries are required.
